title: Active & Empathetic Listening
shortDefinition: A structured communication technique that requires fully hearing, understanding, responding, and remembering what is being said without premature advice.
dailyExample: Responding to an upset friend with: 'It sounds like you felt really dismissed during that meeting, is that right?' instead of immediately offering 5 unsolicited fixes.
psychologyTheory: Grounded in Carl Rogers' Person-Centered Humanistic Psychology. True empathy requires unconditional positive regard and validating the speaker's emotional reality before problem-solving.
inTherapy: Active listening forms the core bedrock of the therapeutic alliance—allowing the client to feel genuinely seen and validated perhaps for the first time.
practicalTakeaway: Before jumping into problem-solving mode, ask one simple question: 'Do you want to be helped, heard, or hugged right now?'
